assessments.reasoning: The pinned autotools-mirror/autoconf object at 99a48ad6c1e3f446717e1f8fec2fb1ae76b09f2e, lib/autoconf/autoconf.m4, matches the claim’s source digest. The driver identifies itself as part of Autoconf. Its FSF notice at bytes [190,2512) supplies the grant, definitions, FSF-release scope and modification condition.

The pinned License Index admission row at bytes [640,783) covers the FSF’s additional permission for generated scripts. The notice preserves the GPL for all other use of the Autoconf material, identifying the base to which the permission relates.

challenge.method: Under pinned SCES-1.0 §§3–4 and Protocol stage 7, compared autoconf.m4 with elisp-comp at the same commit and tested a modification that could emit previously non-data text even if a sample run never emitted it.
challenge.results: autoconf.m4 addresses generated configure scripts. Its threshold is the potential to copy original non-data text into output. A modifier who makes and distributes such a version must delete the exception notice. The elisp-comp file-inclusion grant has a different object and trigger.

limitations: The 2.0 designation identifies the documentary form. The FSF notice prints no independent exception version number. Formal SPDX template matching and byte equality are outside this finding.
The specimen names GPL version 2 with a later-version election. Other files, affected editions and particular generated scripts require separate assessment.
reasoning: The Autoconf 2.59 autoconf.m4 notice grants permission to copy, distribute and modify generated configure scripts. It defines data and non-data portions and gives a precise condition for extending the exception to a modified Autoconf. This is an additional permission under the Index rule. Historical is the registry’s editorial treatment of this form.
